text: Handling deadlines well requires good planning and clear thinking. First, use time management to break large tasks into smaller steps with realistic dates. Next, prioritization helps you decide what is truly important, so you focus on urgent work first instead of wasting hours on small details. Scope management is also key: if a project grows too big, cut extra features that are not essential. Finally, communicate early with your team or teacher if you are falling behind. Speaking up before the deadline gives others time to help, and it protects your reputation. Good habits and honest communication turn deadline stress into steady progress.
